messages:
Alex: Quick sync — I want to lock priorities for the Console observability work next quarter: dashboards (cost + errors), tracing hooks rollout, cost breakdown per-route, and an initial error analytics surface. Need buy-in on launch criteria and minimal scope.
Maya: +1. Can we rank by customer impact and engineering effort? I have two enterprise asks that want per-route cost reporting.
Priya: For launch criteria, I propose: 1) dashboards show top-10 cost hotspots, 2) tracing hooks available on 3 critical services, 3) error analytics supports grouping by trace id. If any of these fail, mark as beta.
Kevin: FYI, infra constraints: tracing hooks add ~8% CPU on p99 for some services if we sample too aggressively. We need sampling strategy before enabling on Dedicated.
Devon: Customer ask from Acme: they want cost breakdown down to model+route+user tier. That's more than our MVP. Can we scope to route+model first?
Maya: Agreed — route+model first. Add user-tier as a stretch. Also we should define acceptance tests: synthetic load with mixed routes and verify cost attribution within 10% error.
Priya: Regarding dashboards, let's pick two templates: "Cost Hotspots" and "Error Lens". Each must have exportable CSV and an easy filter by model and route.
Alex: Good. Who owns the trace-hook rollout plan? Kevin for infra, Maya for product, Devon for customer validation?
Kevin: I can own infra changes and sampling policy. I'll add a canary plan: enable hook with 0.5% sample -> 5% -> 20% across regions.
Devon: I'll line up Acme and BetaCorp for early access. Need a short doc with how to interpret the cost numbers. I can draft that.
Maya: UX ask: error analytics should surface frequent stack traces grouped by fingerprint and allow one-click jump to traces. Is that feasible with current trace retention?
Kevin: Retention is 7 days by default on hosted, but we can surface aggregated fingerprints beyond retention. Full trace details will be limited if older than retention. We should surface fallbacks in the UI.
Priya: Launch gating: must have canary run (traffic simulation) with no >5% latency regression and no wrong cost attribution. Also define rollback criteria if error grouping false positives >10%.
Alex: Good clear gates. Timeline? Plan for a 6-week alpha then 4-week beta.
Maya: Resourcing: UX needs 2 sprints, infra 3 sprints, product/QA 2 sprints parallel. Might push overall to 10 weeks.
Devon: Customer comms: draft initial playbook + FAQ for beta customers. I'll include known limitations and expected accuracy.
TelemBot: Reminder: telemetry-agent v2.3.1 scheduled for deploy at 2025-11-12 02:00 UTC. Trace hook flags will be gated behind feature flag `trace_hooks_v2`.
Kevin: Thanks, Telemetry. We'll coordinate deploy window. Also note we need a migration plan for older agents.
Priya: Action items: Kevin -> sampling policy + canary timeline; Maya -> dashboard wireframes + filters; Devon -> customer playbook + early adopters list; Alex -> compile acceptance tests and finalize launch gates.
Alex: Ok team — I'll assemble these into a short PRD by EOD tomorrow. If anyone has hard objections to scope (route+model + 3 services + two dashboards), raise now.
Maya: No objections. :+1:
Devon: No objections, will sync with customers.
Kevin: No objections. Will post infra runbook when ready.
Priya: No objections. I'll prepare the acceptance test harness.
Alex: Great — closing this huddle. I'll post the PRD link when done.
